entry.title: Comparing Typeclasses and Modules
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | sm2n.ca | discussion

Typeclasses provide ad-hoc polymorphism, enabling operator overloading and type-based dispatch to allow the same identifiers to be reused across different types. Modules provide modular abstraction through encapsulation, information hiding, and dependency injection, allowing for the recursive decomposition of programs into manageable components.

While these constructs can sometimes be used to emulate one another, they serve different architectural purposes: typeclasses facilitate "programming in the small" by managing localized logic, whereas modules facilitate "programming in the large" through high-level structural organization. The article examines how these mechanisms are implemented in languages such as Haskell, OCaml, Rust, and Elixir, arguing that robust modular abstraction is often more critical for software quality than ad-hoc polymorphism.

entry.title: Differences Between foldl and foldr in Haskell
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | blog.haskell.org | discussion

Haskell's `foldl` and `foldr` functions differ in associativity despite both traversing lists from left to right. While both traverse lists from the left, `foldl` is left-associative and `foldr` is right-associative, which fundamentally changes their behavior in lazy evaluation environments.

In lazy evaluation, `foldl` can lead to linear space complexity by building large, nested thunks, whereas the strict version `foldl'` is recommended for constant-space accumulation. In contrast, `foldr` can facilitate streaming and allow for processing infinite lists when the combining function is lazy in its second argument.

entry.title: FunSQL Explains Data-Oriented vs. Syntax-Oriented SQL Query Builders
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | mechanicalrabbit.github.io | discussion

The article distinguishes between two types of SQL query builders: data-oriented and syntax-oriented. Data-oriented builders—such as FunSQL, EF/LINQ, and dbplyr—treat pipeline nodes as sequential data processing steps, meaning the order of operations directly determines the query's output. Conversely, syntax-oriented builders—such as Active Record and Laravel—treat nodes as components for constructing a SQL syntax tree, making the order of assembly irrelevant to the final query.

Syntax-oriented builders are easier to implement but inherit the rigid clause order and grammatical limitations of SQL. Data-oriented builders attempt to represent complex data transformations through query nesting and SQL pushdown, though they may struggle to support the full breadth of SQL's specialized features. FunSQL is designed specifically to expose the complete expressive power of SQL, including recursive queries and lateral joins, by focusing on data processing semantics rather than syntax-driven construction.

entry.title: TimeLord Generates Seeds for Improbable Python Random Sequences
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | github.com | discussion

TimeLord is a Python demonstration that calculates integer seeds required to produce specific, highly improbable sequences from CPython's MT19937 pseudorandom number generator. By representing the generator's twist and temper operations as linear equations over GF(2), the tool works backward from a desired output—such as 1,000 consecutive coin tosses landing on heads or a specific text message—to find a compatible initial seed.

The tool demonstrates the impact of post-selection and selection bias on statistical observations. Reladraw is a text-based diagramming language that defines layouts through relative positioning statements—such as "above-left of"—rather than using absolute coordinates or automatic layout algorithms. The engine resolves these statements by calculating the tightest arrangement of elements based on specified minimum distances, ensuring a deterministic and predictable rendering.

Optimized for AI agents, the language allows models to modify diagrams by editing text-based instructions rather than managing pixel coordinates or interpreting emergent auto-layouts. Currently in version 0.5.0, the project includes a TypeScript-based parser, resolver, and SVG renderer, with an agent skill available for integration into various coding environments.

entry.title: Bitget Reports $387 Million Security Breach Linked to North Korean Hackers
entry.content:
Techmeme | fortune.com

A security breach at Bitget has resulted in the loss of more than $387 million, marking the largest cryptocurrency hack of the year to date. CEO Gracy Chen stated the exchange suspects North Korean attackers exploited a backend system to trick internal approval mechanisms into authorizing fraudulent withdrawals. The breach targeted the exchange's hot and warm wallets, while its self-custodial Bitget Wallet remained unaffected.

Bitget has paused withdrawals and partnered with Mandiant and SlowMist to investigate the incident. The exchange is offering a recovery-bounty program of up to 5% for successfully recovered funds and confirmed its user protection fund, valued at $464 million, is sufficient to cover the estimated losses. This attack follows a significant surge in crypto theft attributed to North Korean groups, which reportedly stole $2 billion in 2025.
